+---

+# Customer intent: As a tenant administrator, I want to reuse approved baselines so that I can standardize configuration across tenants.
+---
+
+# Configuration baseline templates (Preview)
+
+A configuration baseline template is a reusable baseline definition in Microsoft Entra Tenant Governance. Use Configuration baseline templates to standardize baseline definitions across monitors and deployments.
+
+Configuration management supports operations in the home tenant and in other tenants that are connected through governance relationships. A shared template helps you use the same approved configuration standard for those targets.
+
+The **Templates** page separates configuration baseline templates from governance policy templates and shows each baseline template's version.
+
+:::image type="content" source="../media/tenant-governance-configuration-management/configuration-baseline-templates.png" alt-text="Screenshot of configuration baseline templates with descriptions and version numbers." lightbox="../media/tenant-governance-configuration-management/configuration-baseline-templates.png":::
+
+## Templates, baselines, and snapshots
+
+A baseline is the JSON definition of resources and their expected property values. A snapshot captures actual resource settings at a point in time. A template lets you reuse a reviewed baseline when you create monitors or deployments.
+
+Use the following workflow:
+
+1. Capture current settings in a snapshot or author baseline JSON.
+1. Review the settings and remove or adjust values that shouldn't become part of your standard.
+1. Save the approved baseline as a template.
+1. Use the template to create a monitor or deployment for a selected tenant.
+
+A template doesn't grant permissions or apply settings by itself. A monitor evaluates the baseline; a deployment applies it.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Configuration baseline templates are different from [governance policy templates](governance-policy-templates.md). Governance policy templates define access through governance relationships, not the desired configuration of workload resources.
+
+## Reuse across tenants
+
+Before using a template in another tenant, review tenant-specific resource identifiers, dependencies, and workload availability. A baseline captured in one tenant isn't automatically suitable for every target tenant.
+
+The operation that uses the template must have the required permissions in its target tenant. Monitoring requires read access. Deployments require permissions to change the affected settings.
+
+## Manage versions and approvals
+
+Treat approved template revisions as controlled configuration changes:
+
+- Include a version or revision in your naming convention.
+- Record the owner, approval date, and intended environments.
+- Store reviewed baseline JSON in version control.
+- Validate a revision with a limited target scope before broader use.
+- Review existing monitors and deployments explicitly when adopting a revised template; don't rely on editing a template to update existing operations.
+
+The service creates a new version when you save a template edit. Existing monitors continue using their selected version until you explicitly update them. For a template-linked monitor, use **Apply latest**, when available, to adopt the latest version and review its parameter values.
+
+The service limits the number of versions retained for a template. When the limit prevents a save, the editor attempts to delete the oldest version that no monitor references and retry. If all earlier versions are still referenced, update or delete those monitors before trying again. Keep reviewed baseline JSON in version control for durable change history.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Use configuration baseline templates](how-to-use-configuration-baseline-templates.md).
+- [Create configuration snapshots](how-to-create-snapshots.md).
+- [Create a configuration deployment](how-to-create-configuration-deployment.md).
+- [Create a configuration monitor](how-to-create-monitor.md).

+---
+title: Configuration deployments (Preview)
+description: Learn how configuration deployments apply baseline settings to home and governed tenants in Microsoft Entra Tenant Governance.
+ms.topic: concept-article
+ms.date: 11/12/2026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+# Customer intent: As a tenant administrator, I want to understand deployments so that I can apply approved configuration and handle failures.
+---
+
+# Configuration deployments (Preview)
+
+A configuration deployment applies baseline-defined settings to a target tenant. Use Configuration deployments to apply baseline-defined configuration to the home tenant or governed tenants.
+
+Use deployments to roll out approved settings, establish a known-good configuration, or apply controlled changes. Unlike a monitor, which evaluates configuration, a deployment changes resource settings.
+
+The deployment list shows the source template, target tenant, and status for each deployment.
+
+:::image type="content" source="../media/tenant-governance-configuration-management/configuration-deployments.png" alt-text="Screenshot of configuration deployments with source templates, target tenants, and statuses." lightbox="../media/tenant-governance-configuration-management/configuration-deployments.png":::
+
+## Supported resources
+
+Configuration deployments currently support only the following 23 resource types: 15 Microsoft Entra resources and 8 Exchange resources. This list doesn't apply to resource support for snapshots or monitoring.
+
+### Microsoft Entra resources (15)
+
+- `microsoft.entra.conditionalaccesspolicy`
+- `microsoft.entra.namedlocationpolicy`
+- `microsoft.entra.authorizationpolicy`
+- `microsoft.entra.authenticationmethodpolicy`
+- `microsoft.entra.authenticationmethodpolicyemail`
+- `microsoft.entra.authenticationmethodpolicyfido2`
+- `microsoft.entra.authenticationmethodpolicysms`
+- `microsoft.entra.authenticationmethodpolicyvoice`
+- `microsoft.entra.authenticationmethodpolicyx509`
+- `microsoft.entra.crosstenantaccesspolicyconfigurationdefault`
+- `microsoft.entra.crosstenantaccesspolicyconfigurationpartner`
+- `microsoft.entra.externalidentitypolicy`
+- `microsoft.entra.roledefinition`
+- `microsoft.entra.securitydefaults`
+- `microsoft.entra.tenantdetails`
+
+### Exchange resources (8)
+
+- `microsoft.exchange.accepteddomain`
+- `microsoft.exchange.antiphishpolicy`
+- `microsoft.exchange.casmailboxplan`
+- `microsoft.exchange.hostedcontentfilterpolicy`
+- `microsoft.exchange.mailboxplan`
+- `microsoft.exchange.malwarefilterpolicy`
+- `microsoft.exchange.owamailboxpolicy`
+- `microsoft.exchange.safelinkspolicy`
+
+## Baseline and target tenant
+
+Create a deployment from baseline JSON, a snapshot, or a configuration baseline template. Review the resource properties and dependencies before applying the baseline.
+
+Configuration management supports operations in the home tenant and in other tenants that are connected through governance relationships. For a governed tenant, verify the active relationship, delegated access, and workload permissions. A relationship alone doesn't grant permission to change every resource.
+
+## Deployment status
+
+A deployment is asynchronous. Use its status and resource-level results to determine the outcome.
+
+The deployment list displays **Running** or **Completed**. These lifecycle states don't describe whether every resource was applied successfully. Review the run outcome on **Deployment results**, and use **Resource deployment failures** to inspect errors.
+
+| Execution outcome | Meaning | Next action |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| **In progress** | The deployment is applying configuration. | Wait for completion and review available resource outcomes. |
+| **Successful** | The execution reports successful completion. | Use a monitor to validate alignment with the baseline. |
+| **Partially successful** | Some configuration changes succeeded and others didn't. | Review each failed resource and resolve its error before retrying. |
+| **Failed** | The deployment didn't complete successfully. | Review errors and actual resource state before planning another deployment. |
+
+Don't treat a failed or partially successful deployment as proof that no settings changed. Inspect resource outcomes and the target tenant before retrying. Don't assume that deployment failure rolls back successful changes.
+
+The following details view illustrates a partially successful deployment and its baseline version.
+
+:::image type="content" source="../media/tenant-governance-configuration-management/configuration-deployment-details.png" alt-text="Screenshot of deployment details with the template version and a partial-success status." lightbox="../media/tenant-governance-configuration-management/configuration-deployment-details.png":::
+
+## Validate after deployment
+
+Create or update a monitor for the deployed baseline and target tenant. A successful monitor evaluation provides evidence that the actual configuration aligns with the expected values. Later monitor runs detect changes after deployment.
+
+On **Ongoing monitoring** in the deployment wizard, select **Yes** to create a separate monitor from the same configuration. If monitor creation fails, the deployment can still exist; review the warning and create the monitor separately.
+
+Workload-specific systems remain the source of truth for the resource state.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Create a configuration deployment](how-to-create-configuration-deployment.md).
+- [Use configuration baseline templates](how-to-use-configuration-baseline-templates.md).
+- [Configure configuration management service permissions](how-to-set-up-permissions-tenant-monitoring.md).
+- [View monitor results and manage monitors](how-to-see-monitor-results.md).

+---
+title: Create a configuration deployment (Preview)
+description: Learn how to deploy baseline configuration to home and governed tenants and handle partial or failed deployments in Microsoft Entra Tenant Governance.
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/12/2026
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+# Customer intent: As a tenant administrator, I want to deploy an approved baseline so that I can standardize settings in a target tenant.
+---
+
+# Create a configuration deployment (Preview)
+
+Use Configuration deployments to apply baseline-defined configuration to the home tenant or governed tenants. You can create a deployment from baseline JSON, a snapshot, or a configuration baseline template.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as a [Global Administrator](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#global-administrator).
+- The tenant has licenses for **Tenant Governance Basic** or **Tenant Governance Premium**. See [Microsoft Entra Tenant Governance licensing](licensing.md).
+- A reviewed baseline containing only [resources supported for configuration deployments](configuration-deployments.md#supported-resources) and the settings you want to apply. Currently, only the listed 15 Microsoft Entra and 8 Exchange resource types are supported.
+- Delegated write permissions granted to the Tenant Configuration Management service and administrator roles for the selected workload resources. Deployments run on behalf of the signed-in administrator. Application permissions, service principal role assignments, or monitoring read permissions alone aren't sufficient.
+- For another tenant, an active [governance relationship](governance-relationships.md), required delegated permissions, and workload access in the target tenant.
+
+Review [Tenant Governance licensing](licensing.md) and [Configure configuration management service permissions](how-to-set-up-permissions-tenant-monitoring.md) before starting.
+
+## Start a deployment
+
+To start creating a deployment, follow these steps:
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as a [Global Administrator](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#global-administrator).
+1. Browse to **Tenant Governance**. Under **Tenant management**, select **Configuration deployments** for the home tenant. Under **Other tenants**, select **Configuration deployments** for a governed tenant.
+1. Select **Deploy configuration**.
+
+:::image type="content" source="../media/tenant-governance-configuration-management/configuration-deployments.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the deployment list with the Deploy configuration command and target tenants." lightbox="../media/tenant-governance-configuration-management/configuration-deployments.png":::
+
+## Complete the deployment wizard
+
+Configure the baseline and target tenant:
+
+1. For a governed-tenant deployment, select the target tenant on **Tenants**. This step isn't shown for home-tenant deployments, which use your current tenant.
+1. On **Settings**, enter the deployment name and an optional description.
+1. On **Configuration baseline**, upload baseline JSON, import a snapshot, or select a configuration baseline template.
+1. Review tenant-specific resource references, dependencies, and the settings that the deployment will change.
+1. On **Permissions**, review delegated write permission readiness for the selected workload and tenant. Application permissions and roles assigned to the service principal don't satisfy this check. Separately verify the signed-in administrator's workload roles, which aren't evaluated on this step.
+1. On **Ongoing monitoring**, choose whether to monitor for configuration drift after provisioning. Select **Yes** to create a separate monitor from the same configuration, or **No** to deploy without creating a monitor.
+1. On **Review**, confirm the target tenant, baseline, and ongoing monitoring choice, and select **Deploy configuration**.
+
+Repeat the process for additional governed tenants, reviewing tenant-specific values and permissions for each target.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> A deployment changes resource settings in the selected tenant. Review the baseline and impact before confirming, particularly when deploying settings captured from a different tenant.
+
+## Track deployment status
+
+Open the deployment details and refresh to track progress. The deployment list shows **Running** or **Completed** for the deployment lifecycle. **Completed** doesn't establish that every resource was deployed successfully. Open **Deployment results** to review execution outcomes and **Resource deployment failures** to investigate failed resources.
+
+| Status | What to do |
+| --- | --- |
+| **In progress** | Track progress until the deployment completes. |
+| **Successful** | Validate the resulting configuration with a monitor. |
+| **Partially successful** | Identify successful changes and review errors for failed resources. |
+| **Failed** | Review error details and actual resource state before another attempt. |
+
+A failed or partially successful deployment doesn't prove that no changes were applied. Don't assume successful changes were rolled back.
+
+The details view shows the baseline version, target tenant, and deployment outcome.
+
+:::image type="content" source="../media/tenant-governance-configuration-management/configuration-deployment-details.png" alt-text="Screenshot of deployment details showing the target tenant, baseline version, and execution status." lightbox="../media/tenant-governance-configuration-management/configuration-deployment-details.png":::
+
+## Handle failed or partially successful deployments
+
+To address deployment errors, follow these steps:
+
+1. Open the deployment details and identify failed resources and their errors.
+1. Review which resources succeeded and confirm their current state in the target tenant.
+1. Resolve the reported permission, dependency, or baseline issues. For another tenant, also verify the governance relationship and delegated access.
+1. Review the baseline against the current tenant state before attempting changes again.
+1. For a completed home-tenant deployment, use **Redeploy** to apply its stored configuration again. For a governed-tenant deployment, use the configuration update flow or create a new deployment; a standalone **Redeploy** action isn't available.
+1. Review the new outcome, then use a monitor to verify baseline alignment.
+
+An accepted configuration update isn't proof that another deployment execution completed. Refresh the deployment and check **Deployment results** before submitting the same change again.
+
+## Verify the deployed configuration
+
+Create or update a [configuration monitor](how-to-create-monitor.md) for the deployment baseline and target tenant. Review a completed monitor run and any remaining drift.
+
+If you selected **Yes** on **Ongoing monitoring**, verify that the separate monitor was created. A warning that ongoing monitoring couldn't be created doesn't undo the deployment. Resolve the monitor error and create a monitor separately if needed.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Configuration deployments](configuration-deployments.md).
+- [Use configuration baseline templates](how-to-use-configuration-baseline-templates.md).
+- [Create configuration snapshots](how-to-create-snapshots.md).
+- [View monitor results and manage monitors](how-to-see-monitor-results.md).

+---

+description: Learn how to create, edit, version, and apply configuration baseline templates to monitors and deployments in Microsoft Entra Tenant Governance.
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.date: 11/12/2026
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+# Customer intent: As a tenant administrator, I want to manage reusable baseline templates so that I can use approved settings in monitors and deployments.
+---
+
+# Use configuration baseline templates (Preview)
+
+Use Configuration baseline templates to standardize baseline definitions across monitors and deployments. A template contains reusable baseline JSON; selecting it doesn't apply configuration until you create a deployment.
+
+Configuration management supports operations in the home tenant and in other tenants that are connected through governance relationships.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as a [Global Administrator](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#global-administrator).
+- The tenant has licenses for **Tenant Governance Basic** or **Tenant Governance Premium**. Basic includes templates for home-tenant and cross-tenant configuration management. See [Microsoft Entra Tenant Governance licensing](licensing.md).
+- Baseline JSON or a completed snapshot that contains the resource settings you want to reuse.
+- Required workload permissions for operations that use the template. For deployments or monitors in another tenant, an active governance relationship and required delegated access.
+
+For permission setup, see [Configure configuration management service permissions](how-to-set-up-permissions-tenant-monitoring.md).
+
+## Create a template
+
+To create a reusable baseline template, follow these steps:
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as a [Global Administrator](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#global-administrator).
+1. Browse to **Tenant Governance** > **Templates** > **Configuration Baseline Template**.
+1. Select **New configuration template**.
+1. In the **Configuration JSON** editor, provide the template metadata and baseline by uploading a JSON file, importing a completed snapshot, or composing JSON.
+1. Review resource properties and tenant-specific references. If you imported a snapshot, verify that the captured settings represent your intended standard.
+1. Select **Validate + Save**.
+
+:::image type="content" source="../media/tenant-governance-configuration-management/configuration-baseline-templates.png" alt-text="Screenshot of the Templates page with configuration baseline templates and the creation command." lightbox="../media/tenant-governance-configuration-management/configuration-baseline-templates.png":::
+
+## Edit a template
+
+To update template metadata or its baseline, follow these steps:
+
+1. Open the template from **Configuration Baseline Template**.
+1. Update the template metadata or baseline in the **Configuration JSON** editor.
+1. Select **Save changes**.
+
+Saving an edit publishes a new template version. Review the monitors and deployments that should use the revised definition. Changing a template doesn't automatically update existing monitors or reapply configuration to tenants.
+
+## Apply a template to a monitor
+
+To monitor a tenant against the template baseline, follow these steps:
+
+1. Browse to **Tenant Governance**. Under **Tenant management**, select **Monitors** for the home tenant, or under **Other tenants**, select **Monitors (Preview)** for a governed tenant. Select **New monitor**.
+1. For a governed-tenant monitor, select the target on **Tenants**.
+1. On **Configuration baseline**, choose the template option and select the approved template.
+1. Review the baseline and target tenant, then complete permission checks and the remaining steps in [Create a configuration monitor](how-to-create-monitor.md).
+
+## Apply a template to a deployment
+
+To apply the template baseline to a tenant, follow these steps:
+
+1. Browse to **Tenant Governance**. Under **Tenant management** or **Other tenants**, select **Configuration deployments** for the required scope, and select **Deploy configuration**.
+1. For a governed-tenant deployment, select the target on **Tenants**.
+1. On **Configuration baseline**, choose the template option and select the approved template.
+1. Review the settings, tenant-specific references, and write permissions before completing [Create a configuration deployment](how-to-create-configuration-deployment.md).
+
+## Manage template versions
+
+Template edits create service-managed versions. Keep reviewed baseline JSON in version control, and record an owner, approval date, and intended environments for each approved revision.
+
+Test a revision with a limited tenant scope before broader deployment. When replacing an existing baseline, explicitly review and update affected monitors or create deployments from the approved revision. Preserve a copy of the previous baseline for comparison and change review.
+
+For a template-linked monitor, the baseline is read-only in the monitor details. Edit the source template, then use **Apply latest**, when available, to adopt the latest version. Review and supply any required parameter values before confirming.
+
+If the service's template version limit is reached, the editor attempts to delete the oldest version that no monitor references and retries the save. If every earlier version is still referenced, update or delete the monitors using those versions before saving again. Keep your own approved baseline history rather than relying on every service version being retained.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Configuration baseline templates](configuration-baseline-templates.md).
+- [Create configuration snapshots](how-to-create-snapshots.md).
+- [Create a configuration monitor](how-to-create-monitor.md).
+- [Create a configuration deployment](how-to-create-configuration-deployment.md).

See [Remote Desktop Gateway with the NPS extension](howto-mfa-nps-extension-rdg.md). | +| Other VPN deployments with NPS. | Use Microsoft Authenticator push notifications, or TOTP only where the client and authentication protocol support it. Test a replacement path that meets your security requirements. + + + +## Prepare your organization + +Complete the following before the applicable retirement rollout starts: + +1. **Find affected users and applications.** Identify SMS/voice-only users and users whose only alternative is a device-bound passkey unavailable on another device they need. Check whether registered alternatives work in each required sign-in environment. Include NPS/RADIUS and apps that don't support passkeys. +1. **Choose a sign-in path for each scenario.** Prefer passkeys where supported. +# Understand agent SSO, provisioning, and authorization
+
+AI agents increasingly need to access third-party applications and services. Applications use different approaches to authenticate agents, represent agent identities, provision permissions, and authorize access.
+
+Microsoft Entra Agent ID helps organizations manage, govern, and protect AI agent identities. **Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant (ID-JAG)** enables delegated authorization across applications. We'd like to understand how your application supports agent identity and access today and what you plan to support in the future.
+
+If you're familiar with these capabilities, go directly to the [Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant (ID-JAG) | Partner and Customer Interest](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/HWqN80MaeS) form.
+
+## How agent identity and access work
+
+| Capability | What it does |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Microsoft Entra Agent ID** | Manages the agent's identity in Microsoft Entra. |
+| **Agent SSO and authentication** | Authenticates the agent to your application. |
+| **Agent provisioning** | Creates and manages the agent's identity and permissions in your application, when required. |
+| **ID-JAG** | Enables the agent to obtain delegated access to your application. |
+
+## Microsoft Entra Agent ID
+
+Microsoft Entra Agent ID provides identity, security, and governance capabilities for AI agents. Creating an agent identity in Microsoft Entra doesn't automatically create a corresponding identity in your application.
+
+For more information, see [Microsoft Entra Agent ID documentation](index.yml).
+
+## Agent SSO and authentication
+
+Authentication establishes the identity of an agent accessing your application or API. The authentication methods you support depend on your application's identity architecture.
+
+## Agent provisioning
+
+Some applications require an agent to have an identity in their system before access can be granted. For these applications, provisioning creates and manages the agent's identity and permissions.
+
+Provisioning can use SCIM, application-specific APIs, or other mechanisms.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> Provisioning here refers to how the agent is represented and managed in your application, not to creating the agent identity in Microsoft Entra Agent ID.
+
+## ID-JAG
+
+ID-JAG provides delegated authorization to your application. The target application's authorization server validates the grant, applies its authorization policies, and issues an appropriately scoped access token.
+
+## Tell us what your application supports
+
+**Help shape future Microsoft Entra integrations for AI agents.** Tell us how your application supports agent identity and access today, and what you plan to support in the future.
+
+Complete the [Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant (ID-JAG) | Partner and Customer Interest](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/HWqN80MaeS) form to share your application's:
+
+- Agent authentication and SSO capabilities
+- Provisioning approach
+- ID-JAG readiness and plans
+
+We ask about provisioning and ID-JAG separately because they serve different purposes. Provisioning creates and manages an agent's identity and permissions in your application when required. ID-JAG enables delegated authorization to your application. Your application can support either capability without supporting the other.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Sharing this information doesn't commit you to supporting ID-JAG and doesn't mean Microsoft has validated your implementation. Your input helps Microsoft understand partner readiness and inform future integration and testing plans.

 # Update or delete a monitor
 
 This article describes how to update or delete a configuration monitor in the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com). You might update a monitor when your configuration baseline changes. Delete a monitor when the monitored resources are no longer important for your organization's security or compliance requirements.
 
+These actions apply to monitors targeting the home tenant or other tenants connected through governance relationships. Check the monitor's target tenant before updating or deleting it.
+
 ## Prerequisites
 
-- Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [Global Administrator](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#global-administrator).
-- Your tenant must have a license for Microsoft Entra Tenant Governance.
+- Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as a [Global Administrator](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#global-administrator).
+- The tenant has licenses for **Tenant Governance Basic** or **Tenant Governance Premium**. Basic includes monitors targeting the home tenant and governed tenants. See [Microsoft Entra Tenant Governance licensing](licensing.md).
 - At least one configuration monitor must exist in your tenant.
+- For a monitor targeting another tenant, verify the governance relationship and required delegated permissions. Workload permissions must remain valid for subsequent runs.
 
 ## Update a monitor
 
 To update an existing configuration monitor:
 
-1. Browse to **Tenant Governance** > **Configuration management** > **Monitors**.
-1. Find the monitor you want to update and select the edit (pencil) icon next to its name.
+1. Browse to **Tenant Governance**. Under **Tenant management**, select **Monitors** for the home tenant. Under **Other tenants**, select **Monitors (Preview)** for a governed tenant.
+1. Open the monitor and confirm the target tenant.
+1. Use **Settings** to update its name or description, or **Baseline** to update its configuration.
+
+Review the monitor settings, target tenant, baseline, and permission readiness in the update wizard. You can update the baseline by using JSON, a snapshot, or a configuration baseline template, as available in the wizard. For details about baseline selection and tenant scope, see [Create a configuration monitor](how-to-create-monitor.md).
 
-The update wizard uses the same steps as creating a monitor: **Permissions** → **Configuration baseline** → **Review**.

 > [!IMPORTANT]
-> When you update an existing monitor, Tenant Governance automatically deletes all previously generated monitor results and configuration drifts. The updated monitor records results and drifts again each time it runs.
+> A baseline update hides previous monitor results and drift records. A name or description update is a metadata-only change; it doesn't replace the baseline. Preserve required evidence before changing the baseline.
+

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Purview | Information Protection: Sensitivity labels for Microsoft Entra security groups
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Purview will enable sensitivity labels for Microsoft Entra cloud security groups starting mid-January 2027. This allows applying label-based governance and access policies to these groups, enhancing protection and compliance. Admins must enable this feature separately and ensure proper licensing; labels cannot yet be changed or removed once applied.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 13, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

What and why

Microsoft Purview is introducing sensitivity labels for Microsoft Entra cloud security groups. This capability extends label-based protection currently available for Microsoft 365 groups and SharePoint sites to cloud security groups.

With this change, organizations can apply published Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels directly to security groups and automatically enforce membership and guest access policies when groups are created or labeled. This helps administrators apply governance policies consistently across group types, reduce the risk of oversharing, and support controlled self-service group creation.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 568217.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-January 2027 (previously mid-November 2026) and expected to complete in mid-January 2027 (previously late November 2026)

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Entra administrators
  • Microsoft Purview administrators
  • Organizations that use or plan to use sensitivity labels to govern access to Microsoft Entra security groups

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Purview
  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • Microsoft Entra admin center
  • Azure portal
  • Microsoft Graph
  • PowerShell

What will happen

  • Administrators will be able to apply published Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels to cloud security groups during group creation or after a group has been created.
  • Labels can be assigned through the Microsoft Entra admin center, Azure portal, PowerShell, or Microsoft Graph.
  • Existing sensitivity label functionality for Microsoft 365 groups will remain unchanged.
  • Once a sensitivity label is applied to a security group, the label cannot currently be changed or removed. Support for changing assigned labels will be introduced in a future update.
  • Sensitivity labels can be used to enforce organizational membership and guest access policies for security groups.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required to receive this change.

  • To use sensitivity labels with Microsoft Entra security groups after rollout:
  • Confirm that your organization has eligible licensing, such as Microsoft 365 E3 or Microsoft 365 E5, which includes Microsoft Entra ID P1.
  • In the Microsoft Purview portal, publish the sensitivity labels you want to use with the Groups & Sites scope enabled.
  • Allow up to 24 hours for labels to synchronize and become available in Microsoft Entra ID.
  • Enable sensitivity label support for cloud security groups in your tenant settings.
  • If sensitivity labels are already enabled for Microsoft 365 groups, note that cloud security groups require a separate configuration setting and must be enabled independently.

Consider reviewing your existing sensitivity label policies and governance processes before enabling this feature, particularly because assigned labels cannot currently be changed or removed from security groups.

Learn more

  • Assign sensitivity labels to Microsoft Entra security groups | Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn
  • Learn about sensitivity labels | Microsoft Purview | Microsoft Learn
  • Use sensitivity labels to protect collaborative workspaces (groups and sites) | Microsoft Purview | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

QuestionAnswer
Does the change modify or add to Purview-related capabilities?Yes. This update extends Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels to Microsoft Entra security groups, adding a new governance and protection capability for this group type.
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Administrators must enable sensitivity label support for cloud security groups and manage label publication and assignment through Microsoft Purview and Microsoft Entra administrative controls.
Does the change alter how admins manage or demonstrate compliance activities?Yes. Administrators can use sensitivity labels on cloud security groups to apply and enforce access governance policies, expanding the scope of compliance controls available within Microsoft Purview.
